title: A non-affine Steiner design from a differential-spectrum {0,4} function
summary: Determine whether a differentially two-valued {0,4} function can produce a weight-four design inequivalent to the affine-geometry Steiner system.

formal_statement.body: Let $F$ be a binary vectorial function with differential spectrum $\{0,4\}$, and form the source-defined binary code $C(F)$ and incidence structure $(P(C(F)^\perp),B_4(C(F)^\perp))$. Construct an admissible $F$ for which this incidence structure is not equivalent to the Steiner system arising from affine geometry, or prove that every such $F$ yields an equivalent Steiner system.

scope.domain: Differentially two-valued binary functions and the weight-four incidence structures of their associated codes
assumptions: Design equivalence uses the source incidence-structure convention
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected construction produces a provably inequivalent weight-four Steiner design from this differential-spectrum class, and no theorem proves affine-geometry equivalence for every admissible function.

progress.summary: The source asks whether a differential-spectrum {0,4} function can yield a Steiner design outside the affine-geometry equivalence class.
